acceptedWorkstreams.title: Prepare the Product Hunt launch from the things we can actually prove
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The deliverable is the launch copy, the first comment, the maker comment, the asset list and the FAQ, built only from claims we can defend with a link. That means no 'trusted by 10,000+ learners' in the headline, because the homepage figure carries no methodology and a hunter or a commenter will check it. It means the demo is of something a viewer can see working in 30 seconds, and the comparison is framed as a specific swap rather than a 'better than' claim. The asset list is checked against what the site actually serves, so a launch does not point at a screenshot of a feature we have not verified. The launch day FAQ answers the awkward questions, which is the part that decides a launch's comments.

upvotes.reason: Specific and deliverable: it builds the launch copy, first comment, maker comment, asset list and FAQ only from claims defensible with a link, with no unverified statistics in the headline. The asset list is checked against what the site actually serves. That is the right order for a Product Hunt launch.

Supports Zedu's technical marketing and cohort operations roadmap by executing: Prepare the Product Hunt launch from the things we can actually prove. The deliverable is the launch copy, the first comment, the maker comment, the asset list and the FAQ.
Building the launch only from claims with a link, and refusing the homepage figure because it carries no methodology, is what keeps a Product Hunt launch defensible when a hunter asks.

Product Hunt communities punish exaggerated launches; preparing the launch page from claims Zedu can actually prove - and saying what is not claimed yet - is both the honest route and the strategically stronger one, since hunters verify everything within minutes.
Building the launch from assets that already exist and can be proven avoids the usual launch page full of claims nobody can back.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Product Hunt kit with every claim checked against the live product, plus a launch-day plan
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Tagline (under 60 characters), description, the gallery (6 images and the order, each from real screens), the maker's first comment telling the honest story of why Zedu exists, and topics. A launch-day checklist: launch time (12:01 am Pacific), who replies to comments and when, and how to share without asking for upvotes (Product Hunt's rules prohibit that, quoted and linked). Every claim in the copy is checked against the live product on the day before launch.

pendingIdeas.title: Make the five gallery frames tell one story: who, the problem, the workspace, the call, the outcome
pendingIdeas.description: Gallery images are the product page on launch day, and a set of unrelated screenshots wastes them. Work: specify five frames with the caption each carries, the exact screen and state, the data shown (no real learners, current plan names) and the order they appear in. Deliver the shot list with captions, the alt text for each, and the note on the two frames that need a real workflow run first to look credible.

upvotes.reason: "Make the five gallery frames tell one story: who, the problem, the workspace, the call, the outcome" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Plan the day after: where the traffic lands and which page it must not be
pendingIdeas.description: Most launch traffic arrives after the front page, from a link someone shared, and it usually lands on the homepage, which explains the product but not the offer. Work: choose the one destination that matches a launch visitor's intent (a template gallery or a cohort setup guide), check its title, canonical and heading, and write the path from it to a workspace. Deliver the destination, the reason, the metadata check, and the two links in the launch copy that must point there.

upvotes.reason: "Plan the day after: where the traffic lands and which page it must not be" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Prepare answers to the three hostile questions before launch day, not during it
pendingIdeas.description: Every launch draws the same three challenges: naira-only pricing, "another Slack clone", and data handling for minors. Work: write the reply to each in under eighty words, with the fact that answers it and the link that supports it, and decide who is allowed to answer which one. Deliver the three prepared answers, the escalation rule for anything that turns into a security or privacy claim, and the one question the team has not yet agreed an answer to.

upvotes.reason: "Prepare answers to the three hostile questions before launch day, not during it" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Set the launch-day rota and the reply time, because the first six hours decide the ranking
pendingIdeas.description: A launch with unanswered comments loses the momentum it started with. Work: assign named coverage across the first six hours and the following twelve, define the reply window (for example within twenty minutes during coverage), and prepare the holding reply for questions that need the team. Deliver the rota, the reply standard, the holding text, and the escalation path for a comment that alleges a defect during launch.

upvotes.reason: "Set the launch-day rota and the reply time, because the first six hours decide the ranking" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

pendingIdeas.title: Write the first comment as the founder's reason for building Zedu, with one difference stated plainly
pendingIdeas.description: The first comment is the only text most visitors read beyond the tagline, and a feature list there reads like every other launch. Work: draft a short comment in the founder's voice that names the problem (cohorts run in chat apps that were not built for teaching), the one thing Zedu does differently, and one honest limitation, then check each claim against the live product. Deliver the comment, the two alternatives, and the sentences that were cut because they could not be verified.

upvotes.reason: "Write the first comment as the founder's reason for building Zedu, with one difference stated plainly" has a defined audience and a clear done-state, and it addresses something the site does not currently say. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
